c.request: Looking at race results by race name (`races.name`, matched to results by `raceId`), which race names have a total of `points` above the average total across race names? For those race names together, give me in one row their combined total points, their average laps completed, and the average amount by which their totals exceed the average total. For race names with above-average total points, the laps figure is the mean laps over all their individual result rows, so race names with more results weigh more.
c.sql: WITH race_totals AS (SELECT r.name, SUM(res.points) as total_points FROM results res JOIN races r ON res.raceId = r.raceId GROUP BY r.name), avg_total_per_race AS (SELECT AVG(total_points) as avg_total FROM race_totals), above_avg AS (SELECT rt.name, rt.total_points FROM race_totals rt WHERE rt.total_points > (SELECT avg_total FROM avg_total_per_race)) SELECT SUM(aa.total_points) as combined_total_points, (SELECT AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL)) FROM above_avg aa2 JOIN races r ON r.name = aa2.name JOIN results res ON res.raceId = r.raceId) as average_laps, AVG(aa.total_points - (SELECT avg_total FROM avg_total_per_race)) as avg_exceedance FROM above_avg aa

a.request: Matching each result to its race by `raceId`, group by race name (`races.name`) and compute each race name's total `points` and average `laps`. Keep race names whose total points are greater than the average of those totals across all race names. Return one row with: the sum of the kept race names' total points; the average laps across all of their individual results that have a laps value, so race names with more results weigh more; and the average amount by which their totals exceed the average total.
a.sql:
WITH race_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    r.name,
    SUM(res.points) as total_points
  FROM results res
  JOIN races r ON res.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY r.name
),
avg_total_points AS (
  SELECT AVG(total_points) as avg_total FROM race_stats
),
filtered_races AS (
  SELECT 
    rs.name,
    rs.total_points
  FROM race_stats rs
  CROSS JOIN avg_total_points atp
  WHERE rs.total_points > atp.avg_total
)
SELECT
  (SELECT SUM(total_points) FROM filtered_races) as sum_total_points,
  (SELECT AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL)) 
   FROM results res
   JOIN races r ON res.raceId = r.raceId
   JOIN filtered_races fr ON r.name = fr.name
   WHERE res.laps IS NOT NULL AND res.laps != '') as avg_laps,
  (SELECT AVG(fr.total_points - atp.avg_total)
   FROM filtered_races fr
   CROSS JOIN avg_total_points atp) as avg_excess
FROM (SELECT 1)

b.request: For race names whose summed results.points exceeds the mean summed results.points across all race names, return their combined total results.points, the arithmetic mean of results.laps across all individual result rows of those race names, and the arithmetic mean of each qualifying race name's total-point excess above the overall average total.
b.sql:
WITH race_totals AS (
  SELECT races.name, SUM(results.points) as total_points
  FROM races
  JOIN results ON races.raceId = results.raceId
  GROUP BY races.name
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(total_points) as mean_total_points
  FROM race_totals
),
qualifying_races AS (
  SELECT rt.name, rt.total_points, (rt.total_points - oa.mean_total_points) as excess
  FROM race_totals rt, overall_avg oa
  WHERE rt.total_points > oa.mean_total_points
)
SELECT
  (SELECT SUM(total_points) FROM qualifying_races) as combined_total_points,
  (SELECT AVG(CAST(r.laps AS FLOAT))
   FROM qualifying_races qr
   JOIN races ra ON ra.name = qr.name
   JOIN results r ON ra.raceId = r.raceId) as mean_laps,
  (SELECT AVG(excess) FROM qualifying_races) as mean_excess
b.raw: For race names whose summed results.points exceeds the mean summed results.points across all race names, return their combined total results.points, the arithmetic mean of results.laps across all individual result rows of those race names, and the arithmetic mean of each qualifying race name's total-point excess above the overall average total.

d.request: Group results by race name and sum their points per race name; identify those whose sum exceeds the mean of all race names' point sums; report the combined point total for identified races, the mean of individual lap values across all their result rows, and the mean excess of each identified race's total above the overall mean.
d.sql:
WITH race_sums AS (
  SELECT 
    r.name,
    SUM(res.points) as total_points
  FROM results res
  JOIN races r ON res.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY r.name
),
overall_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(total_points) as mean_val FROM race_sums
),
identified AS (
  SELECT 
    rs.name, 
    rs.total_points,
    os.mean_val
  FROM race_sums rs
  CROSS JOIN overall_stats os
  WHERE rs.total_points > os.mean_val
)
SELECT 
  (SELECT SUM(total_points) FROM identified) as combined_point_total,
  AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL)) as mean_lap_values,
  (SELECT AVG(total_points - mean_val) FROM identified) as mean_excess
FROM races r
JOIN results res ON res.raceId = r.raceId
WHERE r.name IN (SELECT name FROM identified)
